stem: Which translator reads one statement, converts it to intermediate code, executes it, then takes the next?
explanation: A compiler reads the whole program; an interpreter stops at the first error.

stem: Which are advantages of an interpreter over a compiler, according to the course?

options.text: Can simulate a machine not yet built

explanation: Compiled programs run ten to a hundred times faster.

stem: Which program merges object files into one executable and resolves references between modules?
explanation: The loader, part of the OS, loads the executable into memory and starts it.

stem: The analysis phase of a compiler is its front end and produces an intermediate representation and the symbol table.
explanation: The synthesis phase (back end) then generates the target program.

stem: A compiler that runs on platform A and generates executable code for platform B is a
explanation: Compiler-compilers generate compilers from a language definition.

stem: Which one is not a logical part of a compiler in the course's diagram?
explanation: The parts are the scanner, analysers, preparation for code generation and code generation, sharing the tables.

stem: What is the difference between a compiler phase and a compiler pass?

options.text: A phase is one stage such as lexical analysis; a pass is a traversal of the whole program and may contain several phases
A pass is one stage; a phase contains several passes
A phase runs only at run time

explanation: Single-pass compilers do all processes in one module.

stem: A compiled source program must be translated again every time it is executed.
explanation: It is translated once; an interpreter translates on every run.
